Situation.Name: Where the numbers live
Situation.Setting: The same dim home workshop at night as before. The 1981 Radio Shack TRS-80 Color Computer sits on the desk in the foreground, keyboard toward the viewer, the beige color composite CRT beside it. A long strip of green-bar fanfold printer paper lies across the desk and spills over its front edge, printed with dense columns of small signed numbers.
Situation.Camera: Mid-shot, slightly low angle across the desk. The computer and the printout fill the lower third of the frame in sharp focus; the character sits behind it, off-centre to the right, leaning over the printout.

CharacterPose.Expression: Concentration with a trace of a smile, lit green by the screen, eyes on the printout
CharacterPose.BodyPosition: Seated behind the desk, leaning forward over the printout
CharacterPose.Gesture: One index finger resting on a single row of numbers on the printout; the other hand flat on the desk beside the keyboard

Article.Name: Stacey's CoCo 1
Article.Description: The exact Radio Shack TRS-80 Color Computer in the reference photo: a wide, low silver-grey case, scuffed and worn from forty-five years of use, with a black recessed keyboard well, small yellowed chiclet keys with dark legends, a red reset key at the top right, a Radio Shack badge with the red, green and blue stripe above the keys, and ventilation slots along the sides. Do not modernise it, clean it, or change its proportions.
Article.Application: Foreground, keyboard toward the viewer, sharp focus, its worn plastic catching the green screen light
Article.SymbolicMeaning: The machine that holds the numbers

Article.Name: Color composite CRT showing the CoCo green raster
Article.Description: A vintage beige composite monitor like the reference photo, with a deep black inner bezel and curved glass. The CoCo display is a bright, nearly rectangular green raster with dark, chunky 8-bit characters in short 32-column rows, this time arranged as a table: a narrow column of short words on the left and three columns of small numbers to the right. Preserve the screen's slight CRT bloom, scan softness and curved-glass reflections. Character shapes should be visible, but individual words and digits should remain too soft to read.
Article.Application: On the desk beside the computer, angled toward the character, the main light source
Article.SymbolicMeaning: The table, on the screen where it lives

Article.Name: Fanfold printout
Article.Description: A long strip of vintage green-bar tractor-feed printer paper with perforated edges and sprocket holes, printed in dot-matrix with dense columns of small signed numbers, softly out of focus except near her fingertip. No headings, no readable words.
Article.Application: Across the desk in front of the keyboard, one end spilling over the desk's front edge toward the viewer, her finger on one row
Article.SymbolicMeaning: The 290 numbers, written out where a person can point at one

Article.Name: Twenty-sided die
Article.Description: A translucent amber d20 catching the neon
Article.Application: Resting on the desk beside the printout, not held
Article.SymbolicMeaning: The roll comes later; this post is about the numbers

KeyDetails: The computer is unmistakably the worn 1981 machine from the reference photo, not a generic retro computer

The CRT faithfully resembles the reference photo: beige cabinet, black bezel, curved glass, and a bright green CoCo raster with dark blocky 32-column characters laid out as a small table of words and numbers
The printout is the focus of her attention: her fingertip on one row, that row alone in sharp focus, the rest of the columns softening away
The die is on the desk, set aside, not in her hand

No readable words anywhere in the image: no signs, posters, slogans, neon lettering, book titles, mug slogans, labels or captions. The CRT and the printout carry only soft, non-legible characters and digits.
No smartwatch, no modern devices, no phone; the only technology in focus is the 1981 machine, its monitor and the printout
Situation.LightingFocus: Green raster glow from the color CRT across the printout, her hands and face; neon rim light separates her from the dark room
